title: Resolution-normalized cohomology maps for coefficient maps on ringed sites
statement:
Let $\mathcal X,\mathcal Y,\mathcal Z$ be sites small in a common coefficient universe, with terminal objects and sheaves of commutative rings $A,B,C$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $f:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal X),A)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal Y),B)$ and $g:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal Y),B)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal Z),C)$ be morphisms of ringed topoi [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Assume the module categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] have enough injectives [def-sp-enough-injectives]. Write $H^q(\mathcal Y,M)=R^q\Gamma(\mathcal Y,-)(M)$, computed in all $B$-modules, and similarly on the other sites. For $B$- and $A$-modules $M,N$ and a $B$-linear coefficient map $\phi:M\to f_*N$, choose nonnegative injective resolutions $N\to I$, $M\to J$, a quasi-isomorphism $\lambda:f_*I\to J'$ to a bounded-below injective complex, and a chain map $\beta:J\to J'$ extending $M\to f_*N\to f_*I\to J'$, with commutation in the homotopy category [def-sp-injective-resolutions, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Then $\Gamma(\mathcal Y,\lambda)$ is a quasi-isomorphism and
$$T_f^q(\phi)=H^q(\Gamma(\mathcal Y,\lambda))^{-1}H^q(\Gamma(\mathcal Y,\beta)):H^q(\mathcal Y,M)\longrightarrow H^q(\mathcal X,N)$$
is independent of all choices. The section identity $\Gamma(\mathcal Y,f_*I)=\Gamma(\mathcal X,I)$, with restriction of scalars, is used in this formula. The map is additive and $\Gamma(\mathcal Y,B)$-linear for its induced action on the target, and $T_f^0(\phi)=\Gamma(\phi)$. For a $C$-module $L$ and $\psi:L\to g_*M$, the canonical section-preserving comparison $(gf)_*\simeq g_*f_*$ gives
$$T_{gf}^q(g_*\phi\circ\psi)=T_f^q(\phi)\circ T_g^q(\psi).$$
These equalities respect geometric $2$-isomorphisms of the composite ringed-topos morphisms with their section-preserving direct-image comparisons. For the identity morphism, $T_{\mathrm{id}}^q(\phi)=H^q(\phi)$; in particular the maps are natural in both coefficient modules.

The normalization also permits computing resolutions: if $M\to K$ and $N\to L'$ are nonnegative resolutions whose terms are acyclic for their respective global-section functors, and $u:K\to f_*L'$ is an augmentation-preserving chain map, the map on section cohomology induced by $u$ equals $T_f^q(\phi)$ under the canonical acyclic-resolution identifications [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity]. In particular, if $f_*I$ resolves $f_*N$, then the map from $H^q(\mathcal Y,f_*N)$ given by the identity coefficient map is the inverse of the acyclic-resolution comparison $H^q(\Gamma(\mathcal Y,f_*I))\to H^q(\mathcal Y,f_*N)$.

For a localization $j:\mathcal X/U\to\mathcal X$ with the restricted ring [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], $T_j^q$ of the unit is the restriction map on cohomology, computed from restriction of sections to $U$. Under the canonical module/abelian evaluation comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-abelian-evaluation-comparison], this is also the ordinary abelian cohomology restriction. No flatness of either structural ring map is assumed.

proof.text: Put $S_{\mathcal T}=\Gamma(\mathcal T,-)$, and write $[v]_q=H^q(S_{\mathcal T}v)$ for a chain map on $\mathcal T$. The adjunction on underlying sheaves gives $\Gamma(\mathcal Y,f_*P)=\operatorname{Hom}(1,f_*P)=\operatorname{Hom}(f^{-1}1,P)=\Gamma(\mathcal X,P)$, naturally in $P$; finite-limit preservation identifies $f^{-1}1=1$. The induced $\Gamma(\mathcal Y,B)$-action is restriction along the structural ring map. Thus this identity applies to differentials, maps and homotopies, not just to objects. Nonnegative injective resolutions and a bounded-below injective replacement of $f_*I$ exist by lem-weil-pbc-complex-injective-resolution-mono. The augmentation $M[0]\to J$ is a degreewise monic quasi-isomorphism, so lem-weil-pbc-lift-along-injective-quasi-iso gives $\beta$ (even with strict augmentation compatibility).

source.place: Tags 013K (lemma-injective-resolutions-exist), 013P(2) (lemma-morphisms-lift); section identities from sites-modules.tex Definition 03D6 (definition-pushforward).

proof.text: Each $f_*I^n$ is $S_{\mathcal Y}$-acyclic by lem-sfb-ringed-topos-injective-pushforward-global-acyclic. Each term of $J'$ is also $S_{\mathcal Y}$-acyclic by clause 1 of lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity. Both complexes are bounded below, so lem-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity-quasi-iso applied to $\lambda$ says $S_{\mathcal Y}\lambda$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Consequently $[\lambda]_q^{-1}[\beta]_q$ exists, with target $H^q(S_{\mathcal X}I)$ by step 1. No assertion that $f_*$ preserves module injectives has been used.

First keep $I,J$ fixed. Every bounded-below injective complex is K-injective by lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective. Given two replacements $\lambda:f_*I\to J'$ and $\widetilde\lambda:f_*I\to\widetilde J'$, the Hom bijection of lem-sp-kinjective-comparison-principle supplies $s:J'\to\widetilde J'$ with $s\lambda\simeq\widetilde\lambda$. The maps $s\beta$ and $\widetilde\beta$ agree after the quasi-isomorphism $M[0]\to J$, hence are homotopic by lem-weil-pbc-lift-to-injective-unique-up-to-homotopy. Homotopies survive sections and give equal cohomology maps by lem-weil-pbc-homotopic-maps-equal-cohomology. Thus $[s]_q[\lambda]_q=[\widetilde\lambda]_q$ and $[s]_q[\beta]_q=[\widetilde\beta]_q$. Step 2 makes both denominators invertible, so $[s]_q$ is invertible and cancellation proves equality of the two roofs. This also proves independence of $\beta$.

source.place: Tags 013P(1), 013S (lemma-morphisms-equal-up-to-homotopy); bounded-below injective comparison in the homotopy category.

proof.text: Now change $I,J$ to $\widetilde I,\widetilde J$. Lift the identity augmentations to $a:I\to\widetilde I$ and $b:J\to\widetilde J$ by lem-weil-pbc-injective-resolution-lift-exists. Reverse lifts exist too; their composites are homotopic to the identities by lem-weil-pbc-lift-to-injective-unique-up-to-homotopy. In particular $f_*a$ is a homotopy equivalence, since direct image is additive. Lift $\widetilde\lambda f_*a$ along $\lambda$ to $s:J'\to\widetilde J'$ using the K-injective Hom bijection. The two maps $s\beta$ and $\widetilde\beta b$ agree up to homotopy after $M[0]\to J$, so they are homotopic. Applying sections gives $[s]_q[\lambda]_q=[\widetilde\lambda]_q[a]_q$ and $[s]_q[\beta]_q=[\widetilde\beta]_q[b]_q$. Cancel as in step 3. The maps $[a]_q,[b]_q$ are precisely the canonical resolution identifications by lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift. This proves independence of all resolutions under those identifications.

source.place: Tags 013P, 013S; injective-resolution formula for higher derived maps, Tag 015B (lemma-higher-derived-functors).

proof.text: All maps in the roof are $\Gamma(\mathcal Y,B)$-linear after step 1's scalar restriction, including the inverse of the isomorphism $[\lambda]_q$. They therefore induce additive linear maps on cohomology. For two coefficient maps use the same $I,J,\lambda$; the sum of their lifts lifts their sum. Step 3 then gives $T_f^q(\phi+\phi')=T_f^q(\phi)+T_f^q(\phi')$, and the zero lift gives zero. In degree zero, left exactness identifies $H^0(S_{\mathcal Y}J)$ and $H^0(S_{\mathcal X}I)$ with sections of $M,N$. The augmentation equation gives $[\beta]_0=[\lambda]_0\Gamma(\phi)$ under these identifications. Cancelling $[\lambda]_0$ proves $T_f^0(\phi)=\Gamma(\phi)$.

source.place: Tag 01FB (remark-explain-arrow), degree-zero augmentation calculation; sites-cohomology.tex section-derived-functors.

proof.text: For the identity morphism take $J'=I$ and $\lambda=\mathrm{id}$. Then $\beta:J\to I$ lifts the ordinary module map $\phi$, and lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift gives $[\beta]_q=H^q(\phi)$ under the chosen resolution identifications. This proves $T_{\mathrm{id}}^q(\phi)=H^q(\phi)$, including the identity coefficient map.

source.place: Tag 015B (lemma-higher-derived-functors); computation of derived maps by resolution lifts.

proof.text:
For composition, keep $I,J,\lambda, eta$ for $f,\phi$, and choose $L	o K$ injective. Choose bounded-below injective replacements $\mu:g_*J	o P$ and $
u:g_*J'	o P'$ by lem-weil-pbc-complex-injective-resolution-mono. Let $\gamma:K	o P$ lift $\psi$ and let $\delta:P	o P'$ satisfy $\delta\mu\simeq
u g_* eta$; the former exists by the monic augmentation lifting theorem, the latter by the K-injective Hom bijection. The normalized statement of lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition applies to the K-injective $I$ and its K-injective replacement $\lambda$ and gives that $g_*\lambda$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Hence $\xi=
u g_*\lambda:g_*f_*I	o P'$ is an allowed injective replacement for the composite. The map $\delta\gamma$ extends $g_*\phi\circ\psi$: after the augmentation from $L$, its homotopy class is $
u g_*\lambda\,g_*f_*(N	o I)\,g_*\phi\,\psi$.

source.place: Tag 0D6E (lemma-derived-pushforward-composition), normalized comparison on injective representatives; derived.tex Tags 013K, 013P.

proof.text:
Write $A=H^q(\Gamma(\mathcal Y,\lambda))$, $B=H^q(\Gamma(\mathcal Y,\beta))$, $C=H^q(\Gamma(\mathcal Z,\mu))$, $D=H^q(\Gamma(\mathcal Z,\gamma))$, $E=H^q(\Gamma(\mathcal Z,\nu))$, and $V=H^q(\Gamma(\mathcal Z,\delta))$. All section comparisons here are step 1's canonical ones, including the given section-preserving $(gf)_*\simeq g_*f_*$. Step 2 makes $A,C,E$ invertible. The homotopy $\delta\mu\simeq\nu g_*\beta$ gives $VC=EB$. Also $H^q(\Gamma(\mathcal Z,\xi))=EA$. Step 7 and independence therefore give
$$T_{gf}^q(g_*\phi\circ\psi)=(EA)^{-1}VD=A^{-1}BC^{-1}D=T_f^q(\phi)T_g^q(\psi).$$
This is cancellation of the displayed six cohomology maps, with no extra coherence claim left implicit.

source.place: Agent calculation of roofs from Tag 0D6E (lemma-derived-pushforward-composition) and cohomology.tex Tag 01FB (remark-explain-arrow).

proof.text: If $\theta:h_*\xrightarrow{\sim}h'_* $ is the direct-image comparison of a geometric 2-isomorphism, use the transported coefficient map $\theta_N\phi$ and replacement $\lambda'=\lambda\theta_I^{-1}:h'_*I\to J'$. Naturality of $\theta$ says $\lambda' h'_*(N\to I)\theta_N\phi=\lambda h_*(N\to I)\phi$, so the same $\beta$ works. Since $\theta_I$ preserves the canonical section comparison, the two section roofs coincide. Independence in steps 3–4 removes these transported choices. Apply this to the composite comparisons of steps 7–8. Finally apply composition with an identity morphism on either side: for $a:M'\to M$ and $b:N\to N'$, it gives $T_f^q(\phi a)=T_f^q(\phi)H^q(a)$ and $T_f^q(f_*b\,\phi)=H^q(b)T_f^q(\phi)$. These are the claimed two coefficient naturality statements.

source.place: Agent calculation using naturality of the given section-preserving direct-image comparisons.

proof.text:
For the acyclic resolutions choose comparison maps $a:L'\to I$ over $N$ and $b:K\to J$ over $M$. Their existence follows by lifting along the degreewise monic quasi-isomorphisms $N[0]\to L'$ and $M[0]\to K$ into the injective targets. Their section cohomology maps are the canonical acyclic-resolution isomorphisms of lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity(2). The maps $\lambda f_*a\,u$ and $\beta b$ from $K$ to $J'$ agree after $M[0]\to K$, by the augmentation condition on $u$ and the defining equation of $\beta$; thus they are homotopic by the injective uniqueness theorem. Applying sections and cohomology gives
$$[\lambda]_q[a]_q H^q(\Gamma(u))=[\beta]_q[b]_q.$$
Consequently $[a]_q H^q(\Gamma(u))[b]_q^{-1}=[\lambda]_q^{-1}[\beta]_q$. This is exactly the claimed normalization under the acyclic-resolution identifications. We have not required the terms of $f_*L'$ to be acyclic or its augmentation to be a resolution.

source.place: Tags 013P(2), 013S and 015E; cohomology.tex Tag 01FB, explicit compatibility with acyclic resolutions.

proof.text: If $f_*I$ resolves $f_*N$, take $M=f_*N$, $K=f_*I$, $L'=I$ and $u=\mathrm{id}$ in step 10. The terms of $K$ are acyclic by lem-sfb-ringed-topos-injective-pushforward-global-acyclic, and the terms of $I$ are acyclic by lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity(1). If $c:H^q(\Gamma(\mathcal Y,f_*I))\to H^q(\mathcal Y,f_*N)$ denotes its acyclic-resolution comparison, the equality in step 10 reads $T_f^q(\mathrm{id})c=\mathrm{id}$. Thus $T_f^q(\mathrm{id})=c^{-1}$, with precisely the orientation in the statement.

source.place: Tag 015E and cohomology.tex Tag 01FB; orientation of the acyclic-resolution comparison.

proof.text: For $j:\mathcal X/U\to\mathcal X$, restriction of modules is exact and has exact left adjoint $j_!$ by lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact. It therefore preserves injectives: for a monomorphism $V\to W$ on the slice, $j_!V\to j_!W$ is monic, so every map $V\to j^*I$, adjoint to $j_!V\to I$, extends across $W$ by injectivity of $I$. Hence an injective resolution $M\to I$ restricts to an injective resolution $j^*M\to j^*I$. Use the chain unit $I\to j_*j^*I$ as $u$ in step 10. By the sectionwise formula of def-pur-localized-ringed-site and adjunction, on sections this sends a global section of $I^n$ to its restriction at $U$ in every degree. Step 10 identifies its cohomology map with $T_j^q$ of the unit. It is the ordinary restriction computed from this common resolution.

To check the final abelian comparison, choose an abelian injective resolution $M_{ab}\to E$ on $\mathcal X$. Exactness of forgetting modules makes $M_{ab}\to I_{ab}$ a resolution. Lift to $a:I_{ab}\to E$ over $M_{ab}$ by the monic augmentation lifting theorem. For every object $V$, the terms of $I_{ab}$ are evaluation-acyclic by the general ringed-site statement of lem-sc-injective-module-abelian-acyclic-zariski, despite its historical name. The Leray acyclic-resolution comparison therefore identifies $H^q(a(V))$ with the canonical module/abelian evaluation comparison at $V$ in lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-abelian-evaluation-comparison. The single sheaf chain map $a$ commutes with restriction from the terminal object to $U$, so its two evaluations give a commuting square of complexes. The two horizontal cohomology maps of that square are exactly the section restrictions in step 12, and the vertical ones are those canonical comparisons. Abelian injectives restrict to injectives by the same exact-left-adjoint argument, now using lem-weil-pbc-site-restriction-injectives. Thus the lower map is ordinary abelian cohomology restriction on the slice. This proves the requested compatibility without assuming $I_{ab}$ injective or the ring flat over $\mathbf Z$.
